raw_response.rationale: The study combines a qualitative literature review (n = 44 studies), a doctrinal review of Brazilian water/Indigenous health legislation (Table 2), and descriptive secondary administrative tabulations from SESAI/SIASI (2019) covering Indigenous villages in Tocantins (Tables 3 and 4). Although the Methodology ('Data treatment', p. 4) states that chi-square tests and t-tests (p < 0.05) were used 'where applicable', zero inferential test statistics, p-values, standard errors, or confidence intervals are reported anywhere in the Results, tables, or text. Only descriptive counts and percentages of sanitation infrastructure coverage (17 [10.6%] villages with WSS and sanitary modules, 93 [58%] with WSS only, and 51 [31.8%] without either) and acute diarrheal disease cases are reported, with no empirical hypothesis test or quantitative contrast across a legal/governance exposure.
